Design and write the Sprint 2 migration for InkOS — the booking engine schema. Working dir: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS`. Existing migrations:
- `20260415000001_bootstrap.sql` — profiles, studios, studio_members, locations, subscriptions, audit_log, webhook_events, `auth.user_studio_ids()` + `public.user_studio_ids()` helpers, `handle_updated_at()`, `handle_new_user()`, storage buckets
- `20260415000002_platform_admin.sql` — `profiles.is_platform_admin`
- `20260415000003_location_contact_fields.sql` — `locations.zip`/`phone` + `locations_owner_delete` + `profiles_team_read` + storage folder prefix check

**Sprint 2 migration — create new file `supabase/migrations/20260415000004_booking_engine.sql`:**

Deliver these tables, all with standard template (`id uuid PK gen_random_uuid()`, `studio_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, `created_at/updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` with `handle_updated_at()` trigger, RLS enabled, indexes on every FK + `studio_id`):

1. **`artists`** (user_id is nullable so studios can list non-user artists as placeholders before inviting)
   - `profile_id uuid REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` — nullable
   - `display_name text NOT NULL`
   - `bio text`
   - `portfolio_url text`
   - `avatar_url text`
   - `specialties text[]` — for AI-design style matching later
   - `commission_default_pct numeric(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 50.00 CHECK (commission_default_pct >= 0 AND commission_default_pct <= 100)`
   - `status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','on_leave','archived'))`
   - `sort_order int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - UNIQUE(studio_id, profile_id) WHERE profile_id IS NOT NULL — one profile can be artist at a studio at most once

2. **`services`**
   - `name text NOT NULL`
   - `slug text NOT NULL` — for public booking URL
   - `description text`
   - `duration_min int NOT NULL CHECK (duration_min > 0 AND duration_min <= 1440)`
   - `base_price_cents int NOT NULL CHECK (base_price_cents >= 0)` — store money as cents
   - `deposit_cents int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (deposit_cents >= 0)`
   - `deposit_required boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`
   - `buffer_before_min int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (buffer_before_min >= 0)`
   - `buffer_after_min int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (buffer_after_min >= 0)`
   - `requires_consultation boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`
   - `is_public boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true` — show on public booking page
   - `sort_order int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `color text` — hex color for calendar display (validated text length, NOT hex constraint — lenient)
   - UNIQUE(studio_id, slug)

3. **`service_artists`** (many-to-many — which artists offer which services, with optional per-artist price override)
   - `service_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES services(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `artist_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES artists(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `price_override_cents int` — nullable, uses base_price if null
   - `duration_override_min int` — nullable
   - PRIMARY KEY (service_id, artist_id)
   - RLS via `studio_id` on parent tables

4. **`clients`**
   - `first_name text NOT NULL`
   - `last_name text`
   - `email text`
   - `phone text`
   - `date_of_birth date`
   - `address jsonb`
   - `source text` — how they found the studio
   - `tags text[]` — VIP, allergic, etc
   - `notes text` — quick-notes field; detailed notes go in `client_notes` (Sprint 3)
   - `total_spent_cents int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `total_sessions int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `last_visit_at timestamptz`
   - `consent_minor boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` — flag if client is under-18
   - UNIQUE(studio_id, lower(email)) WHERE email IS NOT NULL — partial unique index
   - Index on studio_id + last_visit_at DESC
   - Full-text search index (simple): `tsvector` generated column on `first_name || last_name || email || phone`

5. **`bookings`** — THE CORE TABLE
   - `client_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` — don't allow deleting a client with bookings
   - `artist_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES artists(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`
   - `service_id uuid REFERENCES services(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` — allow deleting services, but keep booking record
   - `location_id uuid REFERENCES locations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`
   - `scheduled_at timestamptz NOT NULL`
   - `duration_min int NOT NULL CHECK (duration_min > 0)`
   - `end_at timestamptz GENERATED ALWAYS AS (scheduled_at + (duration_min || ' minutes')::interval) STORED`
   - `status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','confirmed','in_progress','completed','cancelled','no_show'))`
   - `price_cents int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` — final price for this booking (can override service base_price)
   - `deposit_cents int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `deposit_paid boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`
   - `deposit_paid_at timestamptz`
   - `deposit_payment_id text` — Dodo payment ID (Sprint 4)
   - `tip_cents int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `cancellation_reason text`
   - `cancelled_at timestamptz`
   - `cancelled_by uuid REFERENCES profiles(id)`
   - `booking_token uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` — for public confirmation/consent URLs, no auth
   - `source text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'internal' CHECK (source IN ('internal','public','waitlist','import'))`
   - `notes text` — studio-internal notes
   - `client_notes text` — notes from client at booking time
   - `metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`
   - UNIQUE on `booking_token`
   - Indexes: `studio_id`, `client_id`, `artist_id`, `service_id`, `scheduled_at`, `(studio_id, scheduled_at)` composite, `(artist_id, scheduled_at)` composite, `booking_token` unique

   **CRITICAL — artist double-booking prevention via `EXCLUDE USING gist`:**
   - Need btree_gist extension (`CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist`)
   - Constraint: `EXCLUDE USING gist (artist_id WITH =, tstzrange(scheduled_at, end_at, '[)') WITH &&) WHERE (status IN ('pending','confirmed','in_progress'))`
   - This prevents active bookings for the same artist from overlapping at the DB level. Cancelled/completed/no_show are excluded so they don't block new bookings.

6. **`booking_photos`**
   - `booking_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `client_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` — denormalized for faster per-client photo gallery queries
   - `storage_path text NOT NULL` — path in `design-assets` bucket
   - `kind text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('reference','before','during','after','healed'))`
   - `caption text`
   - `taken_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`
   - `uploaded_by uuid REFERENCES profiles(id)`
   - Index on booking_id, client_id

7. **`waitlist_entries`**
   - `client_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `service_id uuid REFERENCES services(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`
   - `artist_id uuid REFERENCES artists(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`
   - `preferred_dates daterange` — range of dates client wants
   - `preferred_days_of_week int[]` — 0=Sunday, 6=Saturday
   - `notes text`
   - `status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','offered','booked','expired','cancelled'))`
   - `offered_booking_id uuid REFERENCES bookings(id)`
   - `offered_at timestamptz`
   - `offered_expires_at timestamptz`

8. **`booking_page_settings`** (per-studio, singleton-ish — one row per studio)
   - `cover_image_url text`
   - `intro_headline text`
   - `intro_body text`
   - `featured_service_ids uuid[]`
   - `show_artist_profiles boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`
   - `show_prices boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`
   - `require_deposit_on_public boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`
   - `lead_time_hours int NOT NULL DEFAULT 24 CHECK (lead_time_hours >= 0)` — minimum hours in advance
   - `cancellation_policy text`
   - `aftercare_message text`
   - UNIQUE(studio_id) — one per studio

**RLS policies — every table:**

Tenant-scoped tables (artists, services, service_artists, clients, bookings, booking_photos, waitlist_entries, booking_page_settings):
- SELECT: `studio_id = ANY(public.user_studio_ids())` (for junction table service_artists, check via service.studio_id)
- INSERT: `WITH CHECK (studio_id = ANY(public.user_studio_ids()))`
- UPDATE: `USING (...) WITH CHECK (...)` same scope
- DELETE: `USING (studio_id = ANY(public.user_studio_ids()) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM studio_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND studio_id = <table>.studio_id AND role IN ('owner','admin','receptionist')))` — role-gated for destructive ops

**Public (unauthenticated) read policies — CRITICAL for public booking flow:**
- `studios` — add public SELECT policy reading ONLY when looking up by slug: add policy with `USING (true)` BUT restrict which columns are readable via a view (see below). Simpler: allow all rows to be SELECTed by `anon` role but put the public booking page through a SECURITY DEFINER RPC function `public_get_studio_by_slug(p_slug text)` that returns only safe columns (name, slug, logo_url, brand_color, timezone, locale).
- `services` — public SELECT when `is_public = true` for anon role (via RPC or direct policy)
- `artists` — public SELECT when `status = 'active'` for anon role
- `bookings` — public SELECT via `booking_token` only: `FOR SELECT USING (booking_token = current_setting('request.jwt.claim.booking_token', true)::uuid OR ...)` — actually, simpler: expose via SECURITY DEFINER RPC `public_get_booking_by_token(p_token uuid)` that returns booking + client name + service name + artist name + studio info.
- `booking_page_settings` — public SELECT via RPC

Prefer RPC functions over direct anon policies — safer, explicit, and lets you control column projection. Create these RPCs:
- `public.public_get_studio_by_slug(p_slug text) RETURNS jsonb` — SECURITY DEFINER STABLE
- `public.public_get_services_for_studio(p_studio_id uuid) RETURNS SETOF jsonb` — only public services
- `public.public_get_artists_for_studio(p_studio_id uuid) RETURNS SETOF jsonb` — only active
- `public.public_get_availability(p_artist_id uuid, p_service_id uuid, p_date date) RETURNS jsonb` — returns available slots given artist schedule (stubbed for now — full logic Sprint 6 when schedules land); Sprint 2 version just returns all hours 9am-9pm minus existing booked slots
- `public.public_create_booking(p_token uuid, p_studio_slug text, p_service_id uuid, p_artist_id uuid, p_scheduled_at timestamptz, p_client_data jsonb) RETURNS jsonb` — creates client if not exists (by email), creates booking with status='pending', source='public', returns booking_token. Race-safe via the EXCLUDE USING gist constraint.
- `public.public_get_booking_by_token(p_token uuid) RETURNS jsonb` — returns booking + denorm data for confirmation page
- Grant EXECUTE to `anon` for these 6 functions only

**Also deliver:**
- Trigger: on bookings UPDATE when status → 'completed', update clients.total_sessions, total_spent_cents, last_visit_at
- Trigger: on bookings INSERT (status='pending' or 'confirmed'), set booking_token if null (already DEFAULT)
- Trigger: enforce service_artists.studio_id consistency — both service and artist must belong to same studio (use a CHECK via trigger since we can't reference other table columns in CHECK)
- Seed data comments — no-op seed; seeds happen via onboarding

**Required extensions:**
- `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist` (needed for EXCLUDE USING gist)
- `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm` (for client search)

**Safety rules:**
- CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY — wait, Supabase migrations run in a transaction by default. Use plain `CREATE INDEX` in migrations (Supabase handles concurrency at its level). Document this.
- Use CHECK constraints for enums, NOT Postgres ENUM type
- Every table: RLS enabled + at least one policy (Sage blocks deploy otherwise)
- Storage: `design-assets` bucket already exists from bootstrap — no new buckets needed
- No destructive ALTERs on existing tables

**Deliverables:**
1. Write the complete migration to `supabase/migrations/20260415000004_booking_engine.sql`
2. Update `lib/supabase/types.ts` to include the new tables with exact nullable/type matches (hand-write since Supabase isn't linked yet — user will regenerate later)
3. Write a short handoff to `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/.handoffs/sprint-2-dato-migration.md` with:
   - Table inventory (row counts, critical columns, RLS summary)
   - EXCLUDE USING gist constraint explanation + what it prevents + when it fires
   - Public booking RPC contract (inputs/outputs for each of the 6 functions)
   - Client search strategy (pg_trgm usage)
   - Known gotchas for Koda (e.g., passing `booking_token` through URL params, not trusting client-sent `studio_id`)
4. Report: migration line count, table count, RLS policy count, RPC function count

Do NOT write any API routes or UI — that's Koda's job. Pure database layer.

9	## 1. MIGRATION SAFETY
10	
11	### Naming Convention
12	```
13	supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql
14	```
15	Example: `20260413120000_add_projects_table.sql`
16	
17	### Zero-Downtime Migration Rules
18	
19	**SAFE (no lock, no downtime):**
20	```sql
21	-- Add nullable column
22	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN description text;
23	
24	-- Add column with default (Postgres 11+ is instant)
25	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active';
26	
27	-- Create index concurrently (doesn't lock table)
28	CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_projects_user_id ON projects(user_id);
29	
30	-- Create new table
31	CREATE TABLE project_tags (...);
32	
33	-- Add foreign key (NOT VALID skips validation of existing rows)
34	ALTER TABLE projects ADD CONSTRAINT fk_user
35	  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES auth.users(id) NOT VALID;
36	-- Then validate separately (lighter lock):
37	ALTER TABLE projects VALIDATE CONSTRAINT fk_user;
38	```
39	
40	**DANGEROUS (locks table, causes downtime):**
41	```sql
42	-- ❌ Adding NOT NULL to existing column without default
43	ALTER TABLE projects ALTER COLUMN description SET NOT NULL;
44	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: Add check constraint
45	ALTER TABLE projects ADD CONSTRAINT projects_description_not_null
46	  CHECK (description IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID;
47	ALTER TABLE projects VALIDATE CONSTRAINT projects_description_not_null;
48	
49	-- ❌ Renaming a column (breaks all queries referencing old name)
50	ALTER TABLE projects RENAME COLUMN name TO title;
51	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: Expand-migrate-contract pattern
52	-- 1. Add new column: ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN title text;
53	-- 2. Backfill: UPDATE projects SET title = name WHERE title IS NULL;
54	-- 3. Switch app code to read/write title
55	-- 4. Drop old: ALTER TABLE projects DROP COLUMN name;
56	
57	-- ❌ Changing column type
58	ALTER TABLE projects ALTER COLUMN price TYPE numeric;
59	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: New column + backfill + swap
60	
61	-- ❌ CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY
62	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_user ON projects(user_id);
63	-- ✅ Always: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
64	```

66	### Migration Rollback Strategy
67	
68	Every migration file should have a corresponding rollback comment:
69	```sql
70	-- Migration: 20260413120000_add_projects_table.sql
71	-- Rollback: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS projects CASCADE;
72	
73	CREATE TABLE projects (
74	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
75	  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
76	  name text NOT NULL,
77	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
78	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
79	);
80	```

82	If a migration fails mid-flight:
83	1. Check what was applied: `SELECT * FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 5;`
84	2. Manually fix the state or apply the rollback SQL
85	3. Never delete a migration file that's been applied — create a new migration to undo it

89	## 2. RLS (Row Level Security) — COMPLETE PATTERNS
90	
91	### Pattern A: User-owned data
92	```sql
93	ALTER TABLE projects ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
94	
95	-- Users see only their own projects
96	CREATE POLICY "users_select_own" ON projects
97	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
98	
99	CREATE POLICY "users_insert_own" ON projects
100	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
101	
102	CREATE POLICY "users_update_own" ON projects
103	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id)
104	  WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
105	
106	CREATE POLICY "users_delete_own" ON projects
107	  FOR DELETE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
108	```
109	
110	### Pattern B: Team/org-scoped data
111	```sql
112	-- Members of an org can see org data
113	CREATE POLICY "org_members_select" ON projects
114	  FOR SELECT USING (
115	    org_id IN (
116	      SELECT org_id FROM org_members
117	      WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
118	    )
119	  );
120	
121	-- Only admins can delete
122	CREATE POLICY "org_admins_delete" ON projects
123	  FOR DELETE USING (
124	    org_id IN (
125	      SELECT org_id FROM org_members
126	      WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND role = 'admin'
127	    )
128	  );
129	```
130	
131	### Pattern C: Public read, authenticated write
132	```sql
133	CREATE POLICY "anyone_select" ON blog_posts
134	  FOR SELECT USING (published = true);
135	
136	CREATE POLICY "authors_insert" ON blog_posts
137	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = author_id);
138	
139	CREATE POLICY "authors_update" ON blog_posts
140	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = author_id);
141	```

143	### Pattern D: Service role bypass (for webhooks, background jobs)
144	```sql
145	-- Service role bypasses RLS by default in Supabase
146	-- But if you WANT policies for service role:
147	CREATE POLICY "service_role_all" ON projects
148	  FOR ALL USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');
149	```
150	**In code:** Use `createClient(url, SERVICE_ROLE_KEY)` for webhook handlers and background jobs. NEVER expose service role key to the browser.

152	### RLS Performance Rules
153	```sql
154	-- ❌ SLOW: Subquery in every row check
155	CREATE POLICY "slow_policy" ON data
156	  FOR SELECT USING (
157	    user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM permissions WHERE ...)
158	  );
159	
160	-- ✅ FAST: Use a security definer function + cache
161	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auth.user_org_ids()
162	RETURNS uuid[] AS $$
163	  SELECT COALESCE(
164	    array_agg(org_id),
165	    '{}'::uuid[]
166	  )
167	  FROM org_members
168	  WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
169	$$ LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER STABLE;
170	
171	CREATE POLICY "fast_org_policy" ON data
172	  FOR SELECT USING (org_id = ANY(auth.user_org_ids()));
173	
174	-- Index to support the function
175	CREATE INDEX idx_org_members_user_id ON org_members(user_id);
176	```

209	### Pattern: Auto-update `updated_at`
210	```sql

213	RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$

215	  NEW.updated_at = now();
216	  RETURN NEW;
217	END;
218	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

221	CREATE TRIGGER set_updated_at
222	  BEFORE UPDATE ON projects
223	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_updated_at();

229	RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
230	BEGIN
231	  INSERT INTO public.profiles (id, email, created_at)
232	  VALUES (NEW.id, NEW.email, now());

243	```sql

245	CREATE TABLE audit_log (
246	  id bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
247	  table_name text NOT NULL,
248	  record_id uuid NOT NULL,
249	  action text NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE')),
250	  old_data jsonb,
251	  new_data jsonb,
252	  user_id uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id),
253	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
254	);

257	ALTER TABLE audit_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

259	  FOR ALL USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');

261	-- Generic audit trigger function
262	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.audit_trigger()
263	RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
264	BEGIN
265	  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
266	    INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, record_id, action, old_data, user_id)
267	    VALUES (TG_TABLE_NAME, OLD.id, 'DELETE', to_jsonb(OLD), auth.uid());
268	    RETURN OLD;
269	  ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN
270	    INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, record_id, action, old_data, new_data, user_id)
271	    VALUES (TG_TABLE_NAME, NEW.id, 'UPDATE', to_jsonb(OLD), to_jsonb(NEW), auth.uid());
272	    RETURN NEW;
273	  ELSIF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
274	    INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, record_id, action, new_data, user_id)
275	    VALUES (TG_TABLE_NAME, NEW.id, 'INSERT', to_jsonb(NEW), auth.uid());
276	    RETURN NEW;
277	  END IF;
278	END;
279	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

281	-- Apply to any table that needs audit logging
282	CREATE TRIGGER audit_projects
283	  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON projects
284	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.audit_trigger();

314	
315	### When to Create Indexes
316	```sql
317	-- Rule: Index every column used in WHERE, JOIN, ORDER BY, or RLS policy
318	
319	-- Foreign keys (ALWAYS index these — Postgres doesn't auto-index FKs)
320	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_user_id ON projects(user_id);
321	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_org_id ON projects(org_id);
322	
323	-- Commonly filtered columns
324	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_status ON projects(status);
325	
326	-- Composite index for multi-column filters
327	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_user_status ON projects(user_id, status);
328	
329	-- Partial index (only index rows that matter)
330	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_active ON projects(user_id)
331	  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'active';
332	
333	-- GIN index for JSONB
334	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_metadata ON projects USING GIN (metadata);
335	
336	-- GIN index for full-text search
337	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN fts tsvector
338	  GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', coalesce(name, '') || ' ' || coalesce(description, ''))) STORED;
339	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_fts ON projects USING GIN (fts);
340	
341	-- Trigram index for LIKE/ILIKE searches
342	CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
343	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_name_trgm ON projects USING GIN (name gin_trgm_ops);
344	```

346	### EXPLAIN ANALYZE — How to Read Query Plans
347	```sql
348	EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT TEXT)
349	SELECT * FROM projects WHERE user_id = 'xxx' AND status = 'active';
350	
351	-- GOOD: "Index Scan using idx_projects_user_status"
352	-- BAD: "Seq Scan on projects" → Missing index
353	-- BAD: "Bitmap Heap Scan" on large table → Index exists but too many rows match
354	-- BAD: "Sort" with high cost → Add index for ORDER BY column

358	```sql

360	SELECT
361	  schemaname, tablename, indexname,
362	  idx_scan, idx_tup_read, idx_tup_fetch,
363	  pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexrelid)) AS size
364	FROM pg_stat_user_indexes

381	## 5. SUPABASE REALTIME SUBSCRIPTIONS
382	
383	### Pattern: Subscribe to table changes (React)
384	```tsx
385	'use client'
386	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
387	import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/client'
388	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
389	
390	type Project = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Row']
391	
392	export function useRealtimeProjects(userId: string) {
393	  const [projects, setProjects] = useState<Project[]>([])
394	  const supabase = createClient()
395	
396	  useEffect(() => {
397	    // Initial fetch
398	    supabase
399	      .from('projects')
400	      .select('*')
401	      .eq('user_id', userId)
402	      .then(({ data }) => {
403	        if (data) setProjects(data)
404	      })
405	
406	    // Subscribe to changes
407	    const channel = supabase
408	      .channel('projects-changes')
409	      .on(
410	        'postgres_changes',
411	        {
412	          event: '*',
413	          schema: 'public',
414	          table: 'projects',
415	          filter: `user_id=eq.${userId}`,
416	        },
417	        (payload) => {
418	          if (payload.eventType === 'INSERT') {
419	            setProjects(prev => [...prev, payload.new as Project])
420	          } else if (payload.eventType === 'UPDATE') {
421	            setProjects(prev =>
422	              prev.map(p => p.id === (payload.new as Project).id ? payload.new as Project : p)
423	            )
424	          } else if (payload.eventType === 'DELETE') {
425	            setProjects(prev =>
426	              prev.filter(p => p.id !== (payload.old as Project).id)
427	            )
428	          }
429	        }
430	      )
431	      .subscribe()
432	
433	    // CRITICAL: Cleanup on unmount
434	    return () => {
435	      supabase.removeChannel(channel)
436	    }
437	  }, [userId])
438	
439	  return projects
440	}
441	```
442	
443	### Realtime Rules
444	1. **Always clean up subscriptions** on component unmount (`removeChannel`)
445	2. **Use filters** (`filter: 'user_id=eq.xxx'`) to reduce payload — never subscribe to entire table
446	3. **RLS applies to Realtime** — users only receive changes they're authorized to see
447	4. **Enable Realtime per table** in Supabase Dashboard → Database → Replication
448	5. **Max channels:** ~100 per client connection. Pool carefully.
449	6. **Don't use Realtime for large datasets** — it sends full row payloads. For high-volume, use polling + React Query.
450	
451	### Enable Realtime on a table
452	```sql
453	-- In migration file
454	ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE projects;
455	```

461	### When to Use Edge Functions vs API Routes
462	- **Edge Functions:** Low-latency global execution, Deno runtime, ~50ms cold start. Use for: lightweight webhooks, image transforms, geolocation-based logic.
463	- **Next.js API Routes (on Railway):** Full Node.js, access to BullMQ/Redis, no cold start. Use for: complex business logic, background jobs, AI inference, heavy computation.
464	
465	**Default to API Routes.** Edge Functions only when latency from a specific region matters.

468	```
469	supabase/functions/
470	  my-function/
471	    index.ts        # Entry point
472	    _shared/        # Shared code between functions
473	      cors.ts
474	      supabase.ts

525	
526	### Standard Table Template
527	```sql
528	CREATE TABLE public.{table_name} (
529	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
530	  -- ownership
531	  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
532	  -- OR for org-scoped:
533	  -- org_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES orgs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
534	
535	  -- data columns here
536	
537	  -- timestamps (EVERY table gets these)
538	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
539	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
540	);
541	
542	-- RLS (EVERY table)
543	ALTER TABLE public.{table_name} ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
544	
545	-- Policies (minimum: SELECT + INSERT for owner)
546	CREATE POLICY "{table}_select" ON public.{table_name}
547	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
548	CREATE POLICY "{table}_insert" ON public.{table_name}
549	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
550	CREATE POLICY "{table}_update" ON public.{table_name}
551	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
552	CREATE POLICY "{table}_delete" ON public.{table_name}
553	  FOR DELETE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
554	
555	-- Index foreign keys
556	CREATE INDEX idx_{table}_user_id ON public.{table_name}(user_id);
557	
558	-- Auto-update timestamp trigger
559	CREATE TRIGGER set_{table}_updated_at
560	  BEFORE UPDATE ON public.{table_name}
561	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_updated_at();
562	```

564	### Enum Pattern (use CHECK constraint, not Postgres ENUM)
565	```sql
566	-- ❌ AVOID: Postgres ENUM (can't remove values, migration nightmare)
567	CREATE TYPE project_status AS ENUM ('active', 'archived');
568	
569	-- ✅ USE: CHECK constraint (easy to modify)
570	CREATE TABLE projects (
571	  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
572	    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'archived', 'deleted'))
573	);
574	```

577	```sql
578	-- Use JSONB for user preferences, metadata, settings
579	ALTER TABLE profiles ADD COLUMN preferences jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb;

614	
615	## 8. BACKUP & DISASTER RECOVERY
616	
617	### Supabase Managed Backups
618	- **Pro plan:** Daily backups, 7-day retention
619	- **Team plan:** Daily backups, 14-day retention
620	- **Enterprise:** Point-in-time recovery (PITR), 30-day retention
621	
622	### Manual Backup (before risky migrations)
623	```bash
624	# Dump full database
625	pg_dump $DATABASE_URL --format=custom --no-owner > backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).dump
626	
627	# Dump specific table
628	pg_dump $DATABASE_URL --format=custom --table=public.projects > projects_backup.dump
629	
630	# Restore from backup
631	pg_restore --dbname=$DATABASE_URL --no-owner --clean backup.dump
632	```
633	
634	### Pre-Migration Safety Script
635	```bash
636	#!/usr/bin/env bash
637	set -euo pipefail
638	# Run BEFORE any risky migration
639	
640	echo "Creating pre-migration backup..."
641	pg_dump "$DATABASE_URL" --format=custom --no-owner > "backup_pre_migration_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).dump"
642	echo "Backup complete: $(ls -lh backup_pre_migration_*.dump | tail -1)"
643	
644	echo "Checking current migration state..."
645	psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT version, name FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 5;"
646	
647	echo "Ready to apply migration. Backup is saved."
648	```

652	## 9. TYPE GENERATION WORKFLOW
653	
654	```bash
655	# From local Supabase (development)
656	pnpm supabase gen types typescript --local > lib/supabase/types.ts
657	
658	# From remote Supabase (staging/production)
659	pnpm supabase gen types typescript --project-ref $SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF > lib/supabase/types.ts
660	
661	# Verify types compile
662	pnpm tsc --noEmit
663	```
664	
665	### Using Generated Types
666	```ts
667	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
668	
669	// Table row type
670	type Project = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Row']
671	
672	// Insert type (omits auto-generated fields)
673	type ProjectInsert = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Insert']
674	
675	// Update type (all fields optional)
676	type ProjectUpdate = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Update']
677	
678	// Use in Supabase queries for type safety
679	const { data } = await supabase
680	  .from('projects')
681	  .select('id, name, status')
682	  .returns<Pick<Project, 'id' | 'name' | 'status'>[]>()
683	```
684	
685	**Rule: Regenerate types after EVERY schema change. If TypeScript complains about a column that exists in the database, the types file is stale.**

688	
689	## 10. CONNECTION MANAGEMENT
690	
691	### Supabase Connection Pooling
692	Supabase uses PgBouncer (Supavisor) for connection pooling:
693	- **Port 5432:** Direct connection (limited connections, use for migrations only)
694	- **Port 6543:** Pooled connection (use for application queries)
695	
696	```
697	# .env
698	# For application (pooled)
699	DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres.[ref]:[password]@aws-0-[region].pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres
700	
701	# For migrations (direct)
702	DIRECT_URL=postgresql://postgres.[ref]:[password]@aws-0-[region].pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres
703	```
704	
705	### Connection Limits
706	- **Free:** 60 direct + unlimited pooled
707	- **Pro:** 100 direct + unlimited pooled
708	- **Team:** 200 direct + unlimited pooled
709	
710	If hitting limits: reduce connection pool in application code, use pooled connection URL, close connections after use.
711	
712	---
713	
714	## 11. DEBUGGING DATABASE ISSUES
715	
716	### Empty Query Results (90% of the time: RLS)
717	```sql
718	-- Check if RLS is blocking
719	SET request.jwt.claims = '{"sub": "user-uuid"}';
720	SET role = 'authenticated';
721	SELECT * FROM projects; -- Does this return rows?
722	RESET role;
723	RESET request.jwt.claims;
724	```
725	
726	### Slow Queries
727	```sql
728	-- Find slow queries
729	SELECT query, calls, mean_exec_time, total_exec_time
730	FROM pg_stat_statements
731	ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC
732	LIMIT 10;
733	
734	-- Check missing indexes
735	SELECT
736	  relname AS table,
737	  seq_scan, seq_tup_read,
738	  idx_scan, idx_tup_fetch,
739	  CASE WHEN seq_scan > 0
740	    THEN ROUND(seq_tup_read::numeric / seq_scan, 0)
741	    ELSE 0
742	  END AS avg_rows_per_seq_scan
743	FROM pg_stat_user_tables
744	WHERE seq_scan > 100
745	ORDER BY seq_tup_read DESC;
746	-- High seq_tup_read + low idx_scan = missing index
747	```
748	
749	### Lock Contention
750	```sql
751	-- Check active locks
752	SELECT pid, mode, relation::regclass, granted
753	FROM pg_locks
754	WHERE NOT granted;
755	
756	-- Kill a blocking query (use with caution)
757	SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid);
758	-- Or force: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid);
759	```
760	
761	### Database Size Monitoring
762	```sql
763	-- Total database size
764	SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(current_database()));
765	
766	-- Size per table
767	SELECT
768	  tablename,
769	  pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('public.' || tablename)) AS total,
770	  pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size('public.' || tablename)) AS data,
771	  pg_size_pretty(pg_indexes_size('public.' || tablename)) AS indexes
772	FROM pg_tables
773	WHERE schemaname = 'public'
774	ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size('public.' || tablename) DESC;
775	```

-- =============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.check_service_artist_studio()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_service_studio UUID;
  v_artist_studio  UUID;
BEGIN
  SELECT studio_id INTO v_service_studio FROM public.services WHERE id = NEW.service_id;
  SELECT studio_id INTO v_artist_studio  FROM public.artists  WHERE id = NEW.artist_id;

  IF v_service_studio IS DISTINCT FROM v_artist_studio THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION
      'service_artist cross-studio violation: service belongs to studio % but artist belongs to studio %',
      v_service_studio, v_artist_studio;
  END IF;

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

-- =============================================================
-- EXCLUDE USING gist: Artist double-booking prevention
--
-- This constraint prevents two active bookings for the same artist
-- from having overlapping time ranges at the DATABASE level.
--
-- How it works:
--   - tstzrange(scheduled_at, end_at, '[)') builds a half-open range:
--     starts at scheduled_at, ends just before end_at.
--   - '[)' = inclusive start, exclusive end — so back-to-back bookings
--     that touch (A ends at T, B starts at T) are NOT considered overlapping.
--   - The WITH && operator means "overlaps".
--   - btree_gist lets us mix a scalar uuid column with a range column
--     inside a single GiST index.
--   - WHERE clause: only fires for active statuses. Cancelled / completed /
--     no_show bookings do NOT block new bookings in that slot.
--
-- What it prevents:
--   Artist is booked 2pm-4pm (confirmed). A second INSERT with
--   artist_id=same, scheduled_at=3pm will FAIL immediately with a
--   constraint violation — no application-layer race condition possible.
--
-- When it fires:
--   INSERT and UPDATE on bookings where status IN ('pending','confirmed','in_progress').
--   Changing status to 'cancelled' releases the slot automatically.
-- =============================================================

ALTER TABLE public.bookings
  ADD CONSTRAINT bookings_artist_no_overlap
  EXCLUDE USING gist (
    artist_id WITH =,
    tstzrange(scheduled_at, end_at, '[)') WITH &&
  )
  WHERE (status IN ('pending', 'confirmed', 'in_progress'));

-- TRIGGER: Update client stats when booking completes
-- =============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.update_client_stats()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Fire only when status transitions TO 'completed'
  IF NEW.status = 'completed' AND (OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'completed') THEN
    UPDATE public.clients
       SET total_sessions    = total_sessions + 1,
           total_spent_cents = total_spent_cents + NEW.price_cents + NEW.tip_cents,
           last_visit_at     = GREATEST(last_visit_at, NEW.scheduled_at),
           updated_at        = now()
     WHERE id = NEW.client_id;
  END IF;

  -- Also reverse if status moves OUT of completed (correction scenario)
  IF OLD.status = 'completed' AND NEW.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'completed' THEN
    UPDATE public.clients
       SET total_sessions    = GREATEST(0, total_sessions - 1),
           total_spent_cents = GREATEST(0, total_spent_cents - OLD.price_cents - OLD.tip_cents),
           updated_at        = now()
     WHERE id = NEW.client_id;
    -- Note: last_visit_at is not reversed — computing the true max would require a subquery;
    -- accept minor inaccuracy here, correctable via periodic recalc job (Sprint 7).
  END IF;

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER bookings_update_client_stats
  AFTER UPDATE ON public.bookings
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_client_stats();

-- 4. public_get_availability
--    Sprint 2 stub: returns 30-min slots between 09:00 and 21:00 on p_date
--    minus already-booked active slots for the artist.
--    Full schedule-aware version ships in Sprint 6 (artist_schedules table).

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.public_get_availability(
  p_artist_id  uuid,
  p_service_id uuid,
  p_date       date
)
RETURNS jsonb
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
STABLE
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_duration_min  INT;
  v_studio_tz     TEXT;
  v_artist_studio UUID;
  v_slots         jsonb := '[]'::jsonb;
  v_slot_start    TIMESTAMPTZ;
  v_slot_end      TIMESTAMPTZ;
  v_day_start     TIMESTAMPTZ;
  v_day_end       TIMESTAMPTZ;
BEGIN
  -- Resolve artist studio and timezone
  SELECT a.studio_id, s.timezone
    INTO v_artist_studio, v_studio_tz
    FROM public.artists a
    JOIN public.studios s ON s.id = a.studio_id
   WHERE a.id = p_artist_id
     AND a.status = 'active';

  IF v_artist_studio IS NULL THEN
    RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', 'artist_not_found');
  END IF;

  -- Resolve service duration (use service base duration; override handled client-side)
  IF p_service_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    SELECT duration_min INTO v_duration_min
      FROM public.services
     WHERE id = p_service_id AND studio_id = v_artist_studio;
  END IF;

  -- Default to 60-min slots if service not found or not provided
  IF v_duration_min IS NULL OR v_duration_min <= 0 THEN
    v_duration_min := 60;
  END IF;

  -- Day window in studio timezone: 09:00 – 21:00
  v_day_start := (p_date || ' 09:00:00')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE v_studio_tz;
  v_day_end   := (p_date || ' 21:00:00')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE v_studio_tz;

  -- Walk forward in duration-sized steps, skip slots with active bookings
  v_slot_start := v_day_start;
  WHILE v_slot_start + (v_duration_min || ' minutes')::interval <= v_day_end LOOP
    v_slot_end := v_slot_start + (v_duration_min || ' minutes')::interval;

    -- Check if this slot overlaps any active booking
    IF NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
        FROM public.bookings b
       WHERE b.artist_id = p_artist_id
         AND b.status IN ('pending', 'confirmed', 'in_progress')
         AND tstzrange(b.scheduled_at, b.end_at, '[)') &&
             tstzrange(v_slot_start, v_slot_end, '[)')
    ) THEN
      v_slots := v_slots || jsonb_build_array(
        jsonb_build_object(
          'start', v_slot_start,
          'end',   v_slot_end
        )
      );
    END IF;

    v_slot_start := v_slot_start + (v_duration_min || ' minutes')::interval;
  END LOOP;

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'date',         p_date,
    'artist_id',    p_artist_id,
    'duration_min', v_duration_min,
    'slots',        v_slots
  );
END;
$$;

-- 5. public_create_booking
--    Creates (or reuses) a client record by email, then inserts a booking.
--    Race-safe: the EXCLUDE USING gist constraint on bookings fires here too.
--    Returns booking_token on success or error details on failure.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.public_create_booking(
  p_token       uuid,        -- idempotency token supplied by client UI
  p_studio_slug text,
  p_service_id  uuid,
  p_artist_id   uuid,
  p_scheduled_at timestamptz,
  p_client_data  jsonb       -- {first_name, last_name, email, phone}
)
RETURNS jsonb
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
VOLATILE
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_studio_id   UUID;
  v_client_id   UUID;
  v_duration    INT;
  v_booking_id  UUID;
  v_token       UUID;
  v_deposit     INT;
BEGIN
  -- Resolve studio
  SELECT id INTO v_studio_id
    FROM public.studios
   WHERE slug = p_studio_slug;

  IF v_studio_id IS NULL THEN
    RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', 'studio_not_found');
  END IF;

  -- Validate artist belongs to studio
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.artists
     WHERE id = p_artist_id AND studio_id = v_studio_id AND status = 'active'
  ) THEN
    RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', 'artist_not_available');
  END IF;

  -- Validate service belongs to studio and is public
  IF p_service_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    SELECT duration_min, deposit_cents
      INTO v_duration, v_deposit
      FROM public.services
     WHERE id = p_service_id AND studio_id = v_studio_id AND is_public = true;

    IF v_duration IS NULL THEN
      RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', 'service_not_available');
    END IF;
  ELSE
    v_duration := 60;
    v_deposit  := 0;
  END IF;

  -- Upsert client by email (case-insensitive) within studio
  IF p_client_data->>'email' IS NOT NULL AND trim(p_client_data->>'email') != '' THEN
    -- Try to find existing client
    SELECT id INTO v_client_id
      FROM public.clients
     WHERE studio_id = v_studio_id
       AND lower(email) = lower(trim(p_client_data->>'email'));

    IF v_client_id IS NULL THEN
      INSERT INTO public.clients (
        studio_id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, source
      )
      VALUES (
        v_studio_id,
        coalesce(trim(p_client_data->>'first_name'), 'Guest'),
        nullif(trim(p_client_data->>'last_name'), ''),
        lower(trim(p_client_data->>'email')),
        nullif(trim(p_client_data->>'phone'), ''),
        'public'
      )
      RETURNING id INTO v_client_id;
    END IF;
  ELSE
    -- No email — create anonymous client record
    INSERT INTO public.clients (
      studio_id, first_name, last_name, phone, source
    )
    VALUES (
      v_studio_id,
      coalesce(trim(p_client_data->>'first_name'), 'Guest'),
      nullif(trim(p_client_data->>'last_name'), ''),
      nullif(trim(p_client_data->>'phone'), ''),
      'public'
    )
    RETURNING id INTO v_client_id;
  END IF;

  -- Use provided token as booking_token (idempotency: if same token exists, return it)
  IF p_token IS NOT NULL THEN
    SELECT id, booking_token INTO v_booking_id, v_token
      FROM public.bookings
     WHERE booking_token = p_token;

    IF v_booking_id IS NOT NULL THEN
      RETURN jsonb_build_object(
        'booking_id',    v_booking_id,
        'booking_token', v_token,
        'status',        'existing'
      );
    END IF;
  END IF;

  -- Insert booking — EXCLUDE USING gist will reject overlaps automatically
  BEGIN
    INSERT INTO public.bookings (
      studio_id,
      client_id,
      artist_id,
      service_id,
      scheduled_at,
      duration_min,
      status,
      deposit_cents,
      source,
      booking_token
    )
    VALUES (
      v_studio_id,
      v_client_id,
      p_artist_id,
      p_service_id,
      p_scheduled_at,
      v_duration,
      'pending',
      coalesce(v_deposit, 0),
      'public',
      coalesce(p_token, gen_random_uuid())
    )
    RETURNING id, booking_token INTO v_booking_id, v_token;
  EXCEPTION
    WHEN exclusion_violation THEN
      RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', 'time_slot_unavailable');
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
      RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', SQLERRM);
  END;

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'booking_id',    v_booking_id,
    'booking_token', v_token,
    'status',        'created'
  );
END;
$$;

# Sprint 2 — Dato Handoff: Booking Engine Schema

Migration file: `supabase/migrations/20260415000004_booking_engine.sql`

---

## Table Inventory

| Table | studio_id FK | Critical Columns | RLS Scope |
|-------|-------------|-----------------|-----------|
| `artists` | CASCADE | `profile_id` (nullable), `status`, `specialties[]`, `commission_default_pct` | `user_studio_ids()` |
| `services` | CASCADE | `slug`, `duration_min`, `base_price_cents`, `deposit_cents`, `is_public` | `user_studio_ids()` |
| `service_artists` | (no direct col) | `service_id + artist_id` PK, optional price/duration overrides | `user_owns_service_studio(service_id)` |
| `clients` | CASCADE | `fts` (generated tsvector), `email` partial-unique, `total_sessions`, `consent_minor` | `user_studio_ids()` |
| `bookings` | CASCADE | `end_at` (generated), `booking_token` (unique UUID), `EXCLUDE USING gist` | `user_studio_ids()` |
| `booking_photos` | CASCADE | `client_id` (denormalized), `kind`, `storage_path` | `user_studio_ids()` |
| `waitlist_entries` | CASCADE | `preferred_dates` (daterange), `offered_booking_id` | `user_studio_ids()` |
| `booking_page_settings` | CASCADE | UNIQUE(studio_id) — one row per studio | `user_studio_ids()` |

All 8 tables have:
- RLS enabled with SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE policies
- `created_at` + `updated_at` timestamps + `handle_updated_at()` trigger
- Indexes on every FK column

---

## EXCLUDE USING gist: Artist Double-Booking Prevention

### What it is
A PostgreSQL exclusion constraint on the `bookings` table:

```sql
EXCLUDE USING gist (
  artist_id WITH =,
  tstzrange(scheduled_at, end_at, '[)') WITH &&
)
WHERE (status IN ('pending', 'confirmed', 'in_progress'))
```

### What it prevents
Two active bookings for the same artist whose time ranges overlap cannot coexist in the database. This is enforced at the storage engine level — no application-layer race condition is possible.

Example: Artist booked 14:00-16:00 (confirmed). Attempting to INSERT a booking at 15:00 for the same artist raises `exclusion_violation` immediately.

### The '[)' half-open range
`tstzrange(start, end, '[)')` = inclusive start, exclusive end. Back-to-back bookings that exactly touch (first ends at T, second starts at T) are NOT considered overlapping. This means artists can be booked consecutively with zero gap.

### When it fires
- On INSERT of any booking with status in `('pending', 'confirmed', 'in_progress')`
- On UPDATE that changes `scheduled_at`, `duration_min`, `artist_id`, or `status` to an active value
- Does NOT fire for status `'cancelled'`, `'completed'`, `'no_show'`

### In `public_create_booking` RPC
The function wraps the INSERT in a `BEGIN/EXCEPTION WHEN exclusion_violation` block and returns `{"error": "time_slot_unavailable"}` to the caller. Koda should surface this to the user as "that time is no longer available."

### Requires btree_gist
The `btree_gist` extension is required to combine a scalar UUID column with a range column in a single GiST index. Enabled in this migration.

---

## Public Booking RPC Contract

All 6 functions are `SECURITY DEFINER`. Callable by `anon` and `authenticated` roles. None expose internal `studio_id` from the request body — the studio is always resolved server-side from the slug.

### 1. `public_get_studio_by_slug(p_slug text) → jsonb`
Returns: `{id, name, slug, logo_url, brand_color, timezone, locale}` or `null`
Used by: `app/book/[studioSlug]/page.tsx` — first call to render the page header.

### 2. `public_get_services_for_studio(p_studio_id uuid) → SETOF jsonb`
Returns: array of `{id, name, slug, description, duration_min, base_price_cents, deposit_cents, deposit_required, requires_consultation, color, sort_order}`
Only returns `is_public = true` services. Internal services are never exposed.

### 3. `public_get_artists_for_studio(p_studio_id uuid) → SETOF jsonb`
Returns: array of `{id, display_name, bio, portfolio_url, avatar_url, specialties, sort_order}`
Only returns `status = 'active'` artists. No commission or financial data exposed.

### 4. `public_get_availability(p_artist_id uuid, p_service_id uuid, p_date date) → jsonb`
Returns:
```json
{
  "date": "2026-05-15",
  "artist_id": "...",
  "duration_min": 90,
  "slots": [
    { "start": "2026-05-15T09:00:00+00:00", "end": "2026-05-15T10:30:00+00:00" },
    ...
  ]
}
```
Sprint 2 stub: 09:00–21:00 window in studio timezone, step = service duration, already-booked active slots removed.
Sprint 6 will replace with schedule-aware version (artist_schedules table).

### 5. `public_create_booking(p_token uuid, p_studio_slug text, p_service_id uuid, p_artist_id uuid, p_scheduled_at timestamptz, p_client_data jsonb) → jsonb`
`p_client_data` shape: `{first_name, last_name, email, phone}`

Success response:
```json
{ "booking_id": "...", "booking_token": "...", "status": "created" }
```
Idempotent: if `p_token` already exists as a `booking_token`, returns `{"status": "existing"}`.
Overlap error: `{"error": "time_slot_unavailable"}`

Side effects:
- Upserts a `clients` row (matched by `lower(email)` within studio)
- Inserts a `bookings` row with `status='pending'`, `source='public'`

### 6. `public_get_booking_by_token(p_token uuid) → jsonb`

```json

  "booking_id": "...",
  "booking_token": "...",
  "status": "pending",
  "scheduled_at": "...",
  "end_at": "...",
  "duration_min": 90,
  "price_cents": 15000,
  "deposit_cents": 5000,
  "deposit_paid": false,
  "studio": { "name": "...", "slug": "...", "logo_url": "...", "timezone": "..." },
  "artist": { "display_name": "...", "avatar_url": "..." },
  "service": { "name": "...", "duration_min": 90 },
  "client": { "first_name": "...", "last_name": "...", "email": "..." }
```

## Client Search Strategy

Two complementary search mechanisms are on the `clients` table:

### Full-text search (tsvector)
- Generated column `fts` (STORED) — `to_tsvector('simple', first_name || last_name || email || phone)`
- GIN index `idx_clients_fts`
- Query pattern: `WHERE fts @@ plainto_tsquery('simple', $1)`
- Best for: multi-word queries, finds "Jane Smith" from "jane smith" or "smith jane"

### Trigram similarity (pg_trgm)
- GIN indexes on `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` using `gin_trgm_ops`
- Query pattern: `WHERE first_name % $1` (similarity) or `WHERE first_name ILIKE '%' || $1 || '%'`
- Best for: partial matches, typo tolerance — "Jone" matches "Jones" with similarity ~0.6

### Recommended Koda query for client search:
```sql
SELECT id, first_name, last_name, email, phone
FROM public.clients
WHERE studio_id = $1
  AND (
    fts @@ plainto_tsquery('simple', $2)
    OR first_name  % $2
    OR last_name   % $2
    OR email       ILIKE '%' || $2 || '%'
  )
ORDER BY similarity(first_name || ' ' || coalesce(last_name,''), $2) DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

## Known Gotchas for Koda

### booking_token in URL params
- Store the `booking_token` UUID in the URL: `/book/confirmation?token=<uuid>`
- Never use `booking_id` in public URLs — that's an internal UUID
- The token is globally unique; no `studio_id` scoping needed for public lookups
- Pass it as the `p_token` idempotency key to `public_create_booking` on submit

### Never trust client-sent studio_id
- All public RPCs resolve `studio_id` server-side from `studio_slug` or `artist_id`
- Koda must NOT accept `studio_id` from the browser request body for public booking flows
- `studio_id` is only trusted when it comes from `auth.uid()` via RLS or SECURITY DEFINER

### end_at is GENERATED ALWAYS
- Never include `end_at` in INSERT or UPDATE queries — Postgres computes it
- In the TypeScript Insert/Update types it is intentionally absent
- It IS in the Row type because you can read it

### service_artists has no studio_id column
- RLS uses `user_owns_service_studio(service_id)` helper
- When inserting a service_artist row, the trigger `enforce_service_artist_same_studio` validates that both the service and artist belong to the same studio — it will RAISE EXCEPTION otherwise

### clients.fts is a generated tsvector
- It is NOT a plain text column — do not SELECT it or try to display it
- The TypeScript Row type intentionally omits it (a tsvector has no JS equivalent)
- Use it only in WHERE clauses via `@@ plainto_tsquery(...)`

### waitlist_entries.preferred_dates is a Postgres daterange
- The Supabase JS client returns dateranges as strings: `"[2026-05-01,2026-06-30)"`
- Parse it with a utility function; do not try to cast it directly as a Date
- When inserting: pass as a string in range literal format: `'[2026-05-01,2026-06-30)'`

### Double-booking UX
- `public_create_booking` returns `{"error": "time_slot_unavailable"}` on exclusion_violation
- The booking form should re-fetch availability slots and show an error — not retry silently
- An RPC returning `{"error": ...}` comes back as HTTP 200 (Supabase RPC success), not 4xx — check the `error` key explicitly

### Deposit payment (Sprint 4)
- `deposit_payment_id` is nullable TEXT — Dodo payment ID stored here after payment confirmation
- `deposit_paid` / `deposit_paid_at` are updated by the Dodo webhook handler (not app code)
- Do not build deposit payment UI in Sprint 2; stub the field

### Storage path for booking_photos
- Use the `design-assets` bucket (created in bootstrap migration)
- Path convention: `{studio_id}/{client_id}/{booking_id}/{kind}/{filename}`
- `storage_path` stores the path within the bucket, not the full URL
- Generate signed URLs server-side for display; never expose raw storage paths publicly
